instructions: Call the city or county planning office before you sign anything and ask whether an outpatient substance use day program (SAIOP or SACOT) is a permitted use at the exact address, and under which zoning district.

Confirm the building is classified Group B Business Occupancy for adult SAIOP and SACOT; adolescent day programs cannot sit in Group B and must meet Group E or Group I-4 under the NC State Building Code.

Add contingencies to the lease or purchase contract: zoning approval, DHSR licensure, a clean Fire Marshal inspection, and tenant-improvement consent for full-height, sound-rated partitions and lockable doors on counseling rooms and records storage.

Sketch a dimensioned floor plan of the space to be licensed, with exits and toilets; DHSR requires it plus interior and exterior photos. Show a reception area and private interview space, which 10A NCAC 27G .0304 lists.
Sign only in the exact legal name on your Secretary of State record, and file the executed lease with your credentials repository for DHSR, LME/MCO contracting and insurance.
tips: AUDIT TRAP: DHSR returns incomplete applications to the sender without processing, and the Day Program checklist requires the original local zoning approval letter. A signed lease without it stalls licensure while rent runs.

Counseling room privacy supports substance use record confidentiality. Specify partitions to the ceiling, sound control and lockable records storage, and ask your compliance consultant to map 42 CFR 2.16 (security for records) to the layout.

CCP 8G Peer Support is not on DHSR's licensed-program list, so a peer-support-only site may not trigger DHSR zoning or Fire Marshal paperwork; confirm with your LME/MCO whether it wants a service location documented.

instructions: Contact the planning department that governs the parcel (city if inside municipal limits, otherwise county) and ask for its written zoning verification or use verification letter for an outpatient substance use treatment day program at the exact address.

Submit the request with street address, parcel ID, a one-page description of services (group and individual counseling, no overnight stay, no medication dispensing), expected client census and the lease or purchase contract.

Pay the jurisdiction's fee. Fees vary: Durham charges $58 for a business or use verification letter and $28 for a zoning-district-only letter. Ask whether a special use permit or rezoning could be required.
Review the letter: it must name the address, the zoning district and state the intended use is permitted. If it says not permitted, request a written determination citing the ordinance section.
Send the original letter to DHSR with your Day Program application; a copy is not enough.
tips: AUDIT TRAP: A zoning-district-only letter does not verify the use. DHSR asks for zoning approval or verification that the facility is classified for the intended use, so request the use-specific letter by name.
Administrative zoning determinations can be appealed to the board of adjustment, and G.S. 160D-405 sets a 30-day appeal window, so calendar the letter date if the answer is no.

Describe the program honestly. Planning staff may classify an outpatient treatment clinic differently from a general office; an unclear description can produce a letter that later does not match the DHSR survey.

instructions: Walk the site with the ADA Checklist for Existing Facilities, starting with Priority 1: accessible parking, route from the street, entrance, then Priority 2 to 4 for restrooms and counseling rooms.
Compare findings to the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design and to the NC Accessibility Code in the NC Building Code Chapter 11, which currently references ANSI A117.1-2009.
Remove barriers that are readily achievable under 28 CFR 36.304, such as ramps, curb cuts, door hardware and restroom grab bars, and get landlord written consent before any alteration.
Ask the local Building Official whether renovations need a permit and whether the space is Group B; new construction or alterations must meet new-construction standards.
Save the completed checklist, photos and contractor invoices for surveyors and LME/MCO site reviews.
tips: AUDIT TRAP: Do not rely on the landlord's statement that the building is ADA compliant. The business that serves the public carries Title III duties, so document your own walk-through.
Check every counseling room, group room and at least one restroom for wheelchair maneuvering space; treatment programs commonly fail on single-user restrooms and doors without clear width.
The federal disabled access credit (IRS Form 8826) may offset eligible access costs for small businesses; ask a CPA before relying on it.
contacts: U.S. DOJ ADA Information Line: 800-514-0301, TTY 833-610-1264 (https://www.ada.gov/infoline/)

instructions: Ask a healthcare-focused insurance broker for professional liability quotes at $1,000,000 per occurrence and $3,000,000 annual aggregate, covering the agency and employees, for SAIOP, SACOT and peer support services.
Choose occurrence or claims-made. If claims-made, buy tail coverage of at least three years after contract end or keep a retroactive date on or before the contract start date.
Confirm the carrier is licensed and authorized in North Carolina by the NC Department of Insurance.
Bind the policy and request a certificate of insurance listing your exact legal entity name; send it to the LME/MCO when you apply for network participation.
Calendar renewal: send a new certificate within 10 business days after any policy expires and give 30 days written notice before coverage is cancelled or reduced.
tips: AUDIT TRAP: Alliance states loss of insurance is a basis for payback of services billed during the gap and may end the contract. Never let a policy lapse, even for a day.
The $1M/$3M limit comes from LME/MCO terms (Alliance publishes it), not from the DHSR packet. The DHHS model contract says each LME/PIHP sets the limits, so check every plan you contract with.
Tell the carrier you offer substance use treatment, including adolescents if applicable. Policies that exclude treatment services or professional acts you actually perform can leave you uncovered.

instructions: Request commercial general liability quotes at $1,000,000 per occurrence and $3,000,000 annual aggregate for bodily injury and property damage arising from your operations.
Bundle a commercial property or business owner's policy for contents, equipment and tenant improvements, and match the limits to what your lease requires of the tenant.
Add hired and non-owned auto coverage, or commercial auto at $500,000 per person and per occurrence, if staff will transport clients or drive for peer support work.
Ask the broker about cyber and abuse or molestation coverage. The LME/MCO pages reviewed do not require them, but you will hold sensitive substance use records and serve vulnerable clients.
Bind coverage, collect certificates for the landlord and each LME/MCO, and store policies in the credentials repository.
tips: AUDIT TRAP: Alliance requires auto liability only if you transport enrollees. Decide whether peer support staff or drivers will transport clients, and document the answer before the plan asks.
Landlords usually require general liability and property certificates before key release, so quote this coverage before the lease signing date.
General liability is separate from professional liability. A professional policy generally does not cover a client slipping in the lobby, so carry both.

instructions: Count employees: three or more regularly employed workers trigger coverage under the NC Workers' Compensation Act, and corporate officers count toward the three.

Request a workers' compensation and employer's liability quote from a broker or directly from a carrier; employer's liability should be at least $100,000 each accident, $100,000 each employee for disease and $500,000 policy limit for LME/MCO contracts.
Ask the broker about the NC Rate Bureau assigned risk plan if carriers decline, and decide whether corporate officers will exclude themselves from coverage, which the Industrial Commission permits.
Bind coverage before the first employee starts; keep the certificate and post the NC Industrial Commission Form 17 workplace poster.
Send the certificate to each LME/MCO with your contract package.
tips: AUDIT TRAP: Corporate officers count toward the three-employee test even if they exclude themselves from the policy, so a corporation with two officers and one employee needs coverage. How LLC members are counted is NOT VERIFIED; ask your broker.
Even with fewer than three employees at opening, Alliance lists statutory workers' compensation among its minimum coverage unless waived in writing by the LME/MCO, so get any waiver in writing.
Form 19 is the Employer's Report of Employee's Injury or Occupational Disease to the Industrial Commission; ask your carrier at binding how injuries must be reported and keep the workplace poster up.

instructions: Create a separate payroll holding ledger, or a second bank sub-account, where you transfer each payday's withheld income tax, Social Security and Medicare, plus the employer share, as payroll is run.
Pay federal deposits by EFT on your Form 941 monthly or semiweekly schedule, and file Form 941 quarterly by the last day of the month after quarter end.
Register for NC withholding with Form NC-BR, then file and pay NC-5 or NC-5Q as assigned; NC does not use a depository system for withholding.
Reconcile the ledger to payroll reports each pay period, and have the CPA review it monthly.
tips: AUDIT TRAP: Withheld payroll taxes are held in trust. The IRS can assess the Trust Fund Recovery Penalty against any responsible person who willfully fails to pay them, including officers and employees.
Fund the ledger on payday, not the due date, so slow Medicaid reimbursement cannot spend tax money.
Keep ledger detail with payroll registers; Medicaid and LME/MCO audits ask for payroll records that tie to staff qualification and timesheets.

instructions: Hold an organizational meeting of the governing body: for a corporation this is the board of directors; for other entities the rule says the owner. Adopt a resolution appointing the Facility Director and Clinical Director.

Record minutes with date, attendees, votes and signatures, and adopt the written policies 10A NCAC 27G .0201(a) requires, including delegation of management authority and the quality assurance and improvement plan.
Approve the ownership disclosure of anyone with 5 percent or more control, and the budget, insurance, bank and lease actions already taken.
Store minutes permanently and set a regular meeting schedule, such as quarterly, with minutes for each meeting.
tips: AUDIT TRAP: 10A NCAC 27G .0201(b) requires governing body minutes to be permanently maintained. Missing minutes are a common licensure survey finding.

The governing body under 10A NCAC 27G .0104 is the board of directors for a corporation and the owner in all other cases; an LLC owner or manager should sign as the governing body and document that choice with counsel.
An advisory committee is optional and does not replace the governing body; keep advisory minutes separate.

instructions: Pass a governing body resolution naming one Facility Director and delegating day-to-day management authority in writing under 10A NCAC 27G .0201(a)(1).

Write a signed job description for the director stating education, experience, duties and responsibilities, as 10A NCAC 27G .0202(a) requires; keep it in the personnel file with licensure verification.

For SAIOP and SACOT, the program must be under the direction of an LCAS or CCS, so the Facility Director may need to be a different person than the clinical lead unless one person meets both roles.
Tell DHSR, NCTracks and each LME/MCO whenever the director changes; stale managing-employee information can delay recredentialing.

For CCP 8G, assign a full-time Qualified Professional meeting 10A NCAC 27G .0104 to direct the program; one QP supervises up to 8 CPSS staff.
Verify credentials on the NC Addictions Specialist Professional Practice Board, plus OIG exclusion and Healthcare Personnel Registry checks. Keep primary-source verification in the file.

The app says QP only. A QP is not enough for SAIOP or SACOT leadership: the supervisor must hold LCAS or CCS, or CSI under the CCP.

instructions: Download the DHSR Policy and Procedure Workbook (worksheet rev. 3-20-25) and use it as your table of contents. Write one policy per item and cite the rule number in each header.

Draft governing body policies required by 10A NCAC 27G .0201(a)(1)-(18): delegation of authority, admission and discharge criteria, records, quality assurance, supervision, training, safety, fee collection, and a client grievance policy with review and disposition procedures.

Draft client rights policies from 10A NCAC Subchapter 27D (rights, notice to clients, confidentiality) and Subchapter 27E (limits on restrictive interventions), including how clients are told of rights and how grievances are filed.
Record governing body meeting minutes; 27G .0201(b) requires permanent retention. Adopt the manual by a dated board resolution.
tips: AUDIT TRAP: Surveyors compare policy text to what staff actually do. 27G .0201(a)(18) requires procedures for review and disposition of grievances, so name the reviewer, set deadlines, and keep a grievance log.

instructions: Confirm your service location address in NCTracks exactly matches the building where services are delivered, and that the site is open and staffed during posted hours.

Watch the Office Administrator email for the site visit notice. NC Medicaid uses Public Consulting Group (PCG) for pre-enrollment visits required by 42 CFR 455.432 for moderate and high risk taxonomies.
Have the owner or clinical lead on site with the DHSR license, service descriptions, program schedule and staff list ready.
Make sure the person who meets the visitor can explain the services you enrolled for (SAIOP, SACOT).
If you are asked to reschedule or correct information, respond through the NCTracks Call Center promptly and keep the ticket number.
tips: AUDIT TRAP: If the person at the visit cannot show basic knowledge of the enrolled services, the visit is recorded as a fail, which leads to automatic termination of participation per NC Medicaid's March 2026 provider notice.
Information on the NCTracks record must match what the visitor finds, including address, services and hours. Keep the record current through Manage Change Requests.
Do not schedule the visit around an unfinished buildout. The program should be set up to operate.

instructions: Open the approval letter and the NCTracks Provider Record. Compare the enrollment effective date for each health plan, service location, taxonomy and service against your DHSR license effective date.
Confirm the effective date is not earlier than the date of your required license, certification or accreditation on file.
Check the date is no more than 365 days before the application and no more than 90 days after it.
If the date is wrong, have the Office Administrator submit a Request to Back-Date Enrollment Effective Dates through Manage Change Request, in a single session.
Do not bill or schedule Medicaid services before the date shown on the record.
tips: AUDIT TRAP: Services delivered before the effective date shown on the provider record are not billable. A back-date request cannot precede the license or accreditation begin date on file.
The 2019 NCTracks notice limits approvals to system issues, emergencies or medically necessary services. Backdating is not routine, so set the requested date correctly at the start.
Only the Office Administrator sees the back-date page, and it cannot be saved as a draft.
contacts: NCTracks Call Center: 1-800-688-6696 (https://www.nctracks.nc.gov/content/public/providers/faq-main-page/faq-general.html)

instructions: Decide which clinicians need individual NCTracks records, such as an LCAS or other licensed professional who enrolled as an individual provider. Qualified Professionals and CCS-credentialed supervisors are not separate NCTracks provider types.
Wait until your organization is approved. Newly enrolling organizations must be approved before individuals can affiliate.
Have each individual provider's Office Administrator log in, open Status and Management, select the individual NPI under Manage Change Request and click Update.
Select Add/Update Affiliations, enter your organization NPI, click Lookup NPI, tick the organization and location, then click Add.
Submit the Manage Change Request and confirm the affiliation shows on the individual record.
tips: AUDIT TRAP: Your organization cannot create or change the affiliation. Only the Office Administrator of the individual's record can. The older Medicaid Bulletin says affiliation-related claims deny if not fixed within the stated period.
Affiliation begin dates default to the current date and cannot be changed. Affiliate before the clinician delivers billable services.

A clinician on another organization's record stays there until you become that record's Office Administrator. Alliance says it fills its claim system from daily NCTracks files, so errors here carry into the Tailored Plan network.

instructions: Decide how you will bill NCTracks (Medicaid Direct fee-for-service): direct 837P, a clearinghouse or a billing agent. If using an agent, add it to your NCTracks record through the billing agent option in Manage Change Request.

If submitting 837P directly, sign the Trading Partner Agreement in the NCTracks portal and obtain your Transaction Supplier Number. Email NCMMIS_EDI_Support@gdit.com for the contact form and a Ramp Management invitation.
Run test 837P files in Ramp Management using the Companion Guide, and fix errors until certified.
Request the 835 electronic remittance through the same trading partner setup, then confirm the first production remittance arrives and reconciles to payments.
Submit one low-dollar production claim and trace it through the 835.
tips: AUDIT TRAP: Medicaid Direct claims go to NCTracks, but Tailored Plan and Standard Plan claims go to the plan, not NCTracks. Test each plan's claim route separately.
NC DHHS can require re-testing if a trading partner generates too many errors in production.
Match the service location, taxonomy and NPI on the 837P to the NCTracks record. Mismatches are the usual cause of early denials.

instructions: Build the note template from the DHHS Record Management and Documentation Manual, July 2025 (effective July 8, 2025). Add fields for individual name, record number or Medicaid ID, full date, service name, contact type, place of service and purpose tied to plan goals.
Add required fields for interventions, duration, effectiveness and response to goals, and electronic authentication with date stamp and credentials.
Add CCP-specific fields: for 8G, start and end time for each PSS unit; for SAIOP and SACOT, hours attended each day.
Make group notes require an individual effectiveness entry per person, and enforce documentation within the required timeframe, with late entries flagged.
Write an EHR standard operating procedure and confirm NC Health Connex (NC HIEA) compliance.
tips: AUDIT TRAP: Duration billed must match the duration in the note. Late entries are billable only up to seven business days after the service date; after that the service is not billable.
Group notes need a full note for every person; the intervention can match across members but effectiveness must be individual.
Cursive font in a Word document is not a valid electronic signature. The EHR must record date-stamped authentication at the time the person signs.
contacts: NC DHHS Records Management and Documentation Manual: https://www.ncdhhs.gov/rmdmjuly-2025/download?attachment (use the plan's provider relations line for questions)

instructions: Create a claim-scrubber rule that checks for SAIOP (H0015) and SACOT (H2035) within the same episode of care for the same member, not just the same calendar day.
Allow an exception only on the day of admission or discharge for the program the member is entering or leaving.
Add a rule blocking SAIOP or SACOT billing in the same episode as individual, family or group SUD therapy, except on admission or discharge days.
Block 8G Peer Support at the same time of day as SAIOP or SACOT, though PSS in the same episode is allowed.
Test with sample claims and have the Billing Specialist sign off before go-live.
tips: AUDIT TRAP: The CCP rule is 'same episode of care', not 'same day'. A member can be in only one of SAIOP or SACOT during a treatment episode, apart from the admission or discharge day.
SACOT is for beneficiaries 18 and older with a primary SUD diagnosis; add an age check.
Document each transition between levels of care so the admission or discharge exception can be proven.

instructions: Set the Peer Support (H0038) billing unit as 15 minutes in the EHR charge master. H0038 HQ for group is also 15 minutes, but not telehealth or telephonic eligible.
Build the unmanaged-unit rule: the first 24 units per beneficiary per episode of care need no prior approval; require authorization after that.
Build an authorization rule capping billing at 176 units per 60-day authorization period and 88 units per 30-day period unless a higher approval is on file.
Block overlap with SAIOP, SACOT, partial hospitalization, PSR, respite and ITS at the same time of day.
Do not hard-code 20 units per day or 80 per week unless a Tailored Plan tells you in writing to.
tips: AUDIT TRAP: The 20-unit daily and 80-unit weekly limits do not appear in CCP 8G amended Sept. 1, 2026. Hard-coding unsourced caps can block payable services or hide real limits.
The Sept. 1, 2026 revision of 8G added unmanaged units and prior approval, so older templates are outdated.
Telehealth and telephonic delivery are limited by the policy; check the current 8G and Policy 1-H before enabling remote delivery.

instructions: Set SAIOP H0015 as one unit per day (an event) and require at least 3 hours of documented service that day before the claim can release.
Set SACOT as H2035, one unit per hour, and require at least 4 hours of SACOT that day before any hours can be billed.
Add scheduling checks: SAIOP at least 3 service days per week; SACOT at least 4 hours per day, 5 days per week, 20 hours per week.
Reject claims where billed duration differs from the note.
Test with sample days of 2.5, 3 and 4 hours.
tips: AUDIT TRAP: The SACOT code is H2035, not H2036. A wrong code will deny or be paid incorrectly.
CCP 8A-12 says adolescents may be scheduled for 2 hours per SAIOP service day, but billing requires 3 hours. Do not bill adolescent days under 3 hours without plan confirmation.
SACOT must operate at least 20 hours per week, with no more than two consecutive days without services.
